pluss::note::rep¶

Back to Note Factory API Reference

Signatures¶

Note pluss::note::rep(string_view value, integer_range sizes)
Note pluss::note::rep(string_view value, std::initializer_list<std::int64_t> sizes)

Repeat One String Across A Shape, Value First¶

rep() builds the same result as full — a Note of shape sizes with value in every cell — but takes its arguments in the other order: value first, shape second. It exists for the call sites where the string is the interesting part of the statement and the shape is a short literal tail.

The value-first order is what makes the second overload possible:

pluss::note::rep("-", {5})          // initializer_list shape, no wrapper

Because the shape is the last argument, it can be a braced initializer_list and still bind unambiguously. full, whose shape comes first, always needs a RangeView wrapper around a container. So the rule of thumb is:

  • rep("x", {2, 3}) — shape is a small literal you are writing inline.

  • full(shape_range, "x") — shape is a variable computed elsewhere.

Both produce a UTF-8-mode Note; both follow the same shape rules (non-negative extents, zero extents allowed, rank at most three, validated before allocation). rep with a range argument simply forwards to full.

The name mirrors the idea of “repeat this value into that shape”. It does not repeat the characters of value — rep("ab", {3}) is three cells each holding "ab", not one cell holding "ababab". Character-level repetition is Note::operator* on an existing Note.

Example 1: A Rule Of Dashes¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::note::rep("-", {5})) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[5], dim=1, numel=5, encoding=utf8)
["-", "-", "-", "-", "-"]

Five cells, each the one-character string "-". The initializer_list shape needs no wrapper.

Example 2: A Multi-Character Value Across A Matrix¶

const pluss::Note n = pluss::note::rep("ab", {2, 2});
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["ab", "ab"], 
  ["ab", "ab"]
]

Each cell holds the whole string "ab" — rep repeats the value, not its letters.

See Also¶

  • pluss::note::full: the shape-first spelling of the same operation.

  • pluss::note::empty: rep("", sizes).

  • pluss::note::make: build from the data when the shape is implied.
